notes: Delta +0.46 (with-skill 100% vs baseline 54%). The baselines were strong on their own — even without the skill, every run led with 'measure before changing', so the skill's value is in Pixhaus specifics, not in teaching the mindset.

Discriminating assertions (where the skill clearly won): eval-0 'leads with measure-don't-guess' + 'no rewrite without a measurement caveat' (baseline jumped straight to a rewrite, never mentioned --release or profiling); eval-1 'std::hint::black_box not criterion::black_box' (baseline used the deprecated re-export and pinned criterion 0.5); eval-2 'uses the repo's existing release-with-debug profile' and 'explains how to read a flamegraph' (baseline reinvented a profiling profile and skipped the reading explanation).

Non-discriminating assertions (both configs passed, low signal): 'criterion as dev-dependency', 'harness = false', 'realistic large size', 'diagnoses dirty-region' — capable models already do these. Consider dropping or tightening for iteration 2.

Gap surfaced by the eval-2 baseline: it went deeper than the skill on GPU-side profiling for an egui+wgpu canvas (puffin/puffin_egui in-process flamegraph, PIX/RenderDoc, wgpu timestamp queries, the CPU->GPU full-texture-upload hypothesis). The skill currently only delegates 'CPU compositing -> wgpu' and doesn't mention profiling the GPU side or that the bottleneck may be upload bandwidth, not CPU. Worth adding for a tool whose hot path is often the GPU.
Single run per configuration (no variance data). Pass-rate stddev is 0 by construction; treat the per-eval pass/fail as the signal, not the (absent) variance.

Time/token cost of the skill: with-skill runs averaged ~47s / ~40.8k tokens vs baseline ~43.6s / ~35.3k — the skill adds ~3s and ~5k tokens (reading SKILL.md + cross-links), a reasonable cost for the accuracy gain.
